name: Horde Tier 2 — The Drowned Fen

premise.value: The hero believes he has discovered a battlefield — a deeper layer of the enemy's corruption, defended by endless waves. In truth, The Drowned Fen is a protected wetland refuge filled with amphibians, aquatic creatures, herbalists, and marsh wardens, and the 'waves' are residents arriving from nearby settlements to contain the same armed intruder.

stages.label: Sealed
stages.entryCondition: The hero holds enough 'trophies' — gate seals taken from senior wardens and Heavy Hands emergency responders — to force this tier's gate.
stages.completionCondition: The hero feeds the gate seals into the amulet and forces open a gate that was never meant to open for him.
stages.notes: Trophies are credentials identifying someone trusted to cross realms in a crisis. The hero reads them as keys carried by elite monsters.

stages.label: The alarm
stages.entryCondition: The gate is forced; the hero steps into The Drowned Fen.
stages.completionCondition: The warning bells are ringing across the commons; the first defenders have arrived.
stages.notes: The first wave is local volunteers — herbalists, frog scouts, and fen-dwelling families — not soldiers.

stages.label: The waves rise
stages.entryCondition: The alarm has spread beyond the immediate commons.
stages.completionCondition: Trained wardens have given way to specialists with defensive equipment.
stages.notes: Trained wardens arrive first, then specialists — marsh wardens with reed barriers and current-turning runes. The pauses between waves shrink because news of the attack is spreading and help arrives faster, not because any army is mustering.

stages.label: The champions
stages.entryCondition: The commons' strongest defenders have answered the bells.
stages.completionCondition: The champions fall protecting the injured; the elites — Heavy Hands emergency responders carrying gate seals — drop the next tier's 'trophies.'
stages.notes: Champions position themselves over the wounded. The Heavy Hands' silhouette is deliberately recognizable so frightened civilians know help has arrived; the hero has learned it means loot.

stages.label: Bank or lose
stages.entryCondition: The hero is laden with shards and trophies deep in the commons.
stages.completionCondition: The hero holds E and banks everything through the amulet — or dies first, and the inhabitants recover their property.
stages.notes: Banking moves the loot out through the diplomatic network, beyond its owners' reach. If he dies first, the game says 'Your pot was lost'; the inhabitants say 'Their property was returned.' Stage graph models one run; a fresh run re-enters quest_horde_t2_drowned_fen__stage_1 in-engine.

label.value: Leave the commons and stop ringing the bells

consequences.value: The warning bells fall silent behind him; the residents tend their injured and rebuild what he broke.
The hero's journal records: 'The horde scatters before my might.' His framing, not the truth.

notes: The commons' faction is fac_drowned_fen_commons (no faction field exists on Quest in v1, so it is recorded here). There is no single representative character per commons, so participatingCharacters and characterKnowledge are empty — both are schema-legal defaults. fact_shards_are_domestic_magic therefore reaches the player as a stage reveal (stage_4) instead of through a faction rep's knowledge bucket. As with the rungs, the hero's delusions live in char_protagonist's profile opinions, not in playerInitialKnowledge.
